figures.caption: Figure 1: Representative sample-size phase diagrams for four link–design settings: (a) identity/Beta(a, 1), (b) integral/bounded density ratio, (c) integral/Beta(a, 1) with 2 < a < 3, and (d) derivative/Beta(a, 1). The SLP holds exactly in the SL and TL regions. The red dashed ray marks the equalizing scale where the individual minimax rates match. In (c), the purple dotted ray marks the within-SL transition from n−1 T to (nnT )−1/2. Parameters: (β, a) = (1, 4) in (a), β = 1 in (b), (1, 2.5) in (c), and (2, 6) in (d).
Table 1: Summary of Results I–IV and the bounded-ratio negative result; Cβ(n, nT ) is the identity-link rate at a = 2 + 1/(2β) in (16).

Figure 2: Integral–derivative comparison under uniform designs. (a) Integral candidate SAR for nT = N , n = Nκn with κn = 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 and β = 1. (b) Fixed-target scan at nT = 220; gray triangles show the raw mixed ratio only for 0.6 < κn < 1. (c) Reversed derivative control for the same function pair, with β = 2, n = N , nT = N0.6, and raw joint SAR. Bands are pointwise paired-bootstrap 95% intervals. Dashed and dash–dot guides show theoretical slopes, vertical dotted lines mark theoretical boundaries and the equalizer, and shaded regions mark fitting windows. Full design and display details are in Appendix D.1.

Figure 3: Regression experiments for the integral link under Beta-source designs with a = 1.5, 2.5, 4, β = 1, a fixed 64-dimensional representation, and cumulative bias bounds using the common smoothness radius L = 64. Panels (a)–(c) use nT = N and n = Nκn and show SAR for predeclared mechanism-specific truths; same-color dashed segments are theoretical tail-rate shapes aligned at the first fitted scale. Panels (d)–(f) fix nT = 211 and show finite-library SAR against κn = log n/ log nT ; purple dash–dot curves are aligned theoretical shapes and vertical dotted lines mark the TD boundary, equalizer, mechanism split, and SD boundary when distinct. Panels (e,f) use paired trajectories on grids ending at κn = 1.60, 2.20, respectively. Bands are 95% bootstrap intervals and horizontal dotted lines mark SAR= 1. Full design and quantitative comparisons are in Appendix D.2.
Table 2: Result III: SLP windows and synergistic rates (integral link, Beta(a, 1)).

Figure 4: Integral-link SAR at a = 2, 3 with β = 1 on the fixed three-function library. Panels (a,b) use nT = N , n = Nκn for κn = .70, .90, 1.00; dotted curves are analytic-risk SAR and same-color dash–dot curves are theoretical references aligned once at N0 = 212. Panels (c,d) fix n = 224, 240 and scan κT ; purple dash–dot segments give the n = 240 reference aligned once at κT = 1. Gray vertical lines mark theoretical boundaries and balances, while orange dashed lines mark analytic-risk channel crossings. Markers at κn = 1 use 400 raw-regression repetitions with pointwise 95% percentile-bootstrap bars. The horizontal line is SAR= 1.

Figure 5: Derivative-link longitudinal SAR and full fixed-source scans with β = 2. Columns distinguish raw-regression Monte Carlo (a = 6, left) from surrogate-model Monte Carlo (a = 3.5, right). (a) Finite-library SAR on κT = .40, .45, .50 inside the theoretical SLP window; dashed guides have slopes 1/30, 1/20, 1/30. (b) Logarithmic SLP paths with c = .5, 1, 1.5, 2 and varying effective κT (N); dashed guides show continuous-rate SAR shapes. Same-color dashed guides in (a) and (b) are aligned at the first fitted scale. (c) The fixed-n = 220 scan with a common truth library and source data, including the nT = 2, 3 small-sample diagnostics. The purple dash–dot curve is the continuous local-rate SAR reference without horizontal calibration; orange dashed lines mark observed channel crossings. Gray dotted vertical lines mark asymptotic balances and window endpoints. (d) Full-range scans at three fixed source-information levels; crosses mark analytic source/target equality and dotted lines mark .4, .6. Colored dotted curves in (d) give exact-risk SAR for the surrogate estimators on a finer scan grid, without sampling bands. Solid lines and markers summarize Monte Carlo estimates; bands are pointwise 95% paired-bootstrap intervals within each model. The joint-estimator SAR is shown without truncation below one. In (b,d), nominal N specifies the information level of the coefficient experiment.

Table 3: Numerical summary of selected regression and coefficient-surrogate rate paths. We report the positive risk-decay exponent α̂R = −d log(R̂)/d log N and the SAR exponent α̂S = d log(ŜAR)/d log N ; brackets are paired-bootstrap 95% intervals. Section 4.1 integral rows use candidate mean-risk minima with β = 1 and the six scales 215, . . . , 220; its derivative row uses β = 2, raw joint risk, and 214, 216, 218, 220. Section 4.3 uses β = 2. Section 4.3 fits use the last four raw scales or six coefficient scales. Their reference slopes are computed from the continuous local-rate integral and its one-channel analogues. Other references are asymptotic exponents.

Figure 6: Derivative-link negative controls with β = 2 and 400 Monte Carlo repetitions per configuration. (a) All six raw-regression paths below the threshold, a = 3 < ac = 3.5. (b) All four raw-regression paths at or outside the a = 6 SLP window .30 < κT < .60. (c) Coefficient-surrogate logarithmic paths at a = 3.5 with c = 0 and c = 1.5, where nT ≈ N3/5/(log N)c. (d) All three fixed-power controls at a = 3.5, nT ≈ NκT . Solid curves and markers give MC SAR estimates with pointwise 95% paired-bootstrap bands. Colored dotted curves in (c,d) are exact-risk SARs for the specified surrogate estimators, without sampling bands. Gray horizontal lines mark SAR= 1. Below-threshold finite-range growth and SAR below one are shown without truncation. In (c,d), nominal N denotes coefficient information.

Figure 7: Real-data integral–derivative comparison on IO-VNBD. (a) Observed heading change and the calibrated yaw-rate integral in the deterministically selected median-discrepancy window. (b) Equal-track geometric SAR on the integration middle path and the safeguarded differentiation path. Bands are exploratory 95% track-resampling intervals conditional on the audited windows.

Figure 8: Semi-synthetic unbounded-shift calibration using empirical errors derived from the IO-VNBD signals introduced above. (a) Integration SAR for the q = .45 and q = .60 paths. (b) Differentiation SAR on the primary path and three controls for the sample-size regime, singularity threshold, and bounded density ratio. Bands are pointwise 95% signal-distinct-track bootstrap intervals, and the horizontal dashed lines mark SAR= 1.
